explanation: The tongue is anchored to the hyoid, slim bones that loop over the skull, so it can shoot far out to spear or hook grubs deep in wood.

claims.text: A woodpecker's tongue is supported by a long hyoid apparatus that wraps around the back of the skull when the tongue is drawn in.
Pelicans, parrots and kingfishers do not have a hyoid that wraps around the skull.
The long hyoid lets a woodpecker extend its tongue far beyond its beak to reach insect larvae in wood.
Many woodpeckers have barbed or sticky tongue tips for catching grubs.
